newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - July Coffee still seen struggling at 1,700.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - July Coffee still seen struggling at 1,700.

text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
LIFFE coffee futures could continue drifting lower if July keeps failing to break through stiff resistance at $1,700 per tonne.

July coffee was calculated to open up $120, but traders said they only expected $40 to $50 higher. They said coffee should be limited by strong upside resistance and its recent failures to meet opening call expectations on the upside.
On Thursday, July closed down $18 at $1,644, near the middle of its range.
Because July has consistently failed to sustain gains above lateral resistance at $1,700, Susan Rigg at Chart Analysis said coffee could drift down toward reaction lows near $1,550.
July coffee also continues to hold a gap from Monday's high of $1,705 and the March 12 low of $1,730, which is providing resistance, some analysts noted.
Some traders expected July coffee to remain trapped in a near-term range between $1,620 and $1,700.

Underlying robusta support could come from New York's strong arabicas market. On Thursday, traders there were encouraged by July's strong finish above Wednesday's 196.00 high. They said July could test Monday's contract high at 199.00 in the near-term.

One U.S. analyst pegged his first CSCE July coffee target at 212.00, which he said could come as early as Monday because cycles still looked very bullish. Longer-term cycles were also friendly into late June, he said.
